t: You're looking at St George's, Hanover Square, the Anglican parish church of Mayfair. It was built in the early eighteenth century as part of a project to build fifty new churches around London. John James designed it, and General William Steuart, who donated the site, laid the first stone in 1721. Because of its position near Oxford Circus, it has often hosted society weddings. Among those buried here is Ann Radcliffe, who pioneered the Gothic novel and wrote The Mysteries of Udolpho. Colonial governors Francis Nicholson and Josiah Martin, the last British governor of North Carolina, are buried here too.
